Do operations on events (intersection, union).
Key term: Union
Key term: Intersection
Key term: Two mutually exclusive events
Key term: Venn diagram

If A is an event of S, i.e. A ⊂ S, then P(A) = n(A)/n(S). $P(A)=\frac{n(A)}{n(S)}$
n(A) is the number of elements of the event A, n(S) is the number of elements of sample space S, and P(A) is the probability of occurring event A.
we notice that : probability can be written as a fraction or percentage as follows :
Operations on events :

Events are subset of the sample space (S), so oparetions on events are similar to the operations on sets such as union and intersection. When the sample sapce (S) is considered the universal set, we can represent events and operations on the sample space by using Venn diagrams:
First: intersection
If A and B are two events from a sample space (S), then the intersection of the two events A and B, denoted by the symbol A ∩ B, means the events A and B occur together. $A \cap B$
Note that: It is said that an event occurred if the outcome of the experiment is an element of the elements of the set expressing this event.
The two events B and C cannot occur at the same time so we say B and C are mutually exclusive events.
Mutually exclusive events.
A and B are mutually exclusive events if $A\cap B=\phi$. $A\cap B=\phi$
A set of events is mutually exclusive if every pair of them is mutually exclusive.
A regular dice is rolled once :
Second : Union

If A and B are two events from the sample space S, the union of the two events, denoted $A\cup B$, means the occurrence of the two events A or B or both, i.e. occurrence of at least one event. $A\cup B$
Remark: if A and B are mutually exclusive events from sample space S (as in the figure), then the following hold.
For mutually exclusive events, A ∩ B is the empty set. $A \cap B = \phi$
P(A ∩ B) = (number of elements of φ)/(number of elements of S) = Zero/(number of elements of S) = Zero. $P(A \cap B)=\frac{n(\phi)}{n(S)}=\frac{0}{n(S)}=0$
Notic that A and B are mutually exclusive events. Then P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B) but (A ∩ B) = zero. ∴ P(A ∪ B) = 4/9 + 1/9 - zero = 5/9 As previously found
If A and B are two mutually exclusive events then P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B). $P(A \cup B)=P(A)+P(B)$

Third: use the venn diagram to calculate the probability of: a) Occurrence of A or B; b) Occurrence of A or C; c) Find $P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$, $P(A\cup B)$, what do you notice? steps.text: Third a: Occurrence of A or B means $A\cup B$, where $A\cup B=\{2,3,4,6,8,9\}$, $n(A\cup B)=6$
probability of the occurrence of A or B $=P(A\cup B)=\frac{n(A\cup B)}{n(S)}=\frac{6}{9}=\frac{2}{3}$
Third b: Occurrence of A or C means $A\cup C$, they are two distant sets, then $A\cup C=\{2,4,6,7,8\}$, $n(A\cup C)=5$
probability of the occurrence of A or C $=P(A\cup C)=\frac{n(A\cup C)}{n(S)}=\frac{5}{9}$
from (1) and (2) we get $P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)=P(A\cup B)$

blocks.text: Complementary event and the difference between two events
The concept of the complementary even(t); The concept of the difference between two events.
Key term: complementary event
Key term: difference between two events
In the venn diagram opposite: If S is the universal set, A ⊂ S then the complementary set of A is A`.

From the previous, we notice that: If S is the sample space of a random experiment and one ball is drawn from a box having identical balls numbered from 1 to 7 and observing the number on it. A is the event of getting even number: A = {2, 4, 6}. A` is the event of getting an odd number: A` = {1, 3, 5, 7} and it is a complementary event to A.
The complementry event :
If A ⊂ S then A` is the complementary event to event A, where A ∪ A` = S and A ∩ A` = φ. $A\cup A'=S,\ A\cap A'=\phi$
The event and the complementary event are two mutually exclusive events.

Notice that: The event of reading Al Akhbar newspaper is represented by venn opposite diagram by set A while the event of reading Al Akhbar only but not other newspaper is represented by the set A - B
The set A - B (reading Al Akhbar only, not the other newspaper) is read as 'A difference B'. $A-B$
The difference between two events
If A, B are events of S, then A-B is the event of the occurrence of A and the non-occurrence of B, i.e. the occurrence of the event A only.
Note that (A - B) ∪ (A ∩ B) = A (the symbol between the two brackets is not clearly printed). $(A - B) \cup (A \cap B) = A$

worked_examples.title: example-1
worked_examples.question: A classroom contains 40 students. 18 of them read Al-Akhbar newspaper, 15 read Al Ahram news paper and 8 read both newspapers. If a student is selected randomly calculate the probability that the student: (A) reads Al-Akhbar newspaper (B) doesn't read Al-Akhbar newspaper (C) reads Al-Ahram newspaper (D) reads both newspapers.

steps.text: Let the event A be reading Al Akhbar newspaper and the event B reading Al Ahram newspaper. then A ∩ B is the event of reading both newspapers.
A: event A: Read Al Akhbar newspaper then $P(A)=\frac{n(A)}{n(S)}=\frac{18}{40}=\frac{9}{20}$
B: Does not read Al Akhbar is the complementary event of the event A and it is A`. $\therefore P(A')=\frac{\text{number of elements of s set }A'}{n(S)}=\frac{15+7}{40}=\frac{22}{40}=\frac{11}{20}$
C: event B: read Al Ahram newspaper then: $P(B)=\frac{n(B)}{n(S)}=\frac{15}{40}=\frac{3}{8}$
D: event A ∩ B means reading both newspaper. $\therefore P(A\cap B)=\frac{n(A\cap B)}{n(S)}=\frac{8}{40}=\frac{1}{5}$
